figures.finding: Sri Lanka's National Film Development Fund, set up by Extraordinary Gazette No. 799/1 of 27 December 1993 (amended 1996) and run by a Board of Control at the National Film Corporation (NFC), exists to give financial support and incentives for 'high-quality artistic and commercially successful local films', cinema upgrades and scholarships; its share, cap and selection rate are not published.

value.name: National Film Development Fund (NFC)
value.law: Extraordinary Gazette No. 799/1 (1993-12-27), amended by Gazette No. 946/9 (1996-10-24)

figures.applies: Sri Lanka, local films; page read 2026-11-01.

sources.said: The National Film Development Fund was established with the aim of promoting the development of the local film industry, in accordance with the regulations set forth in the Extraordinary Gazette No. 799/1 dated 1993.12.27, as amended by Gazette No. 946/9 dated 1996.10.24. This Fund is administrated by a Board of Control. The key objectives of the Fund are as follows: To provide financial support and incentives for the production of high-quality artistic and commercially successful local films.

figures.finding: Every Sri Lankan film must be registered with the NFC before production starts, for a fee of Rs 5,000 (Rs 3,000 to change the title), filing the producer's papers, the agreements signed with the main actor, actress, director, cinematographer and editor, the synopsis and the writer's affidavit; a production casting a foreign artiste pays the National Film Development Fund Rs 25,000 for a major role and Rs 10,000 for a supporting role. Foreign shoots need the NFC's permission.

sources.said: Every film should be registered at the National Film Corporation of Sri Lanka before commencing its production. Fee for registration is Rs. 5,000/= . … Copies of the Agreements signed with main Actor, Actress, Director, Cinematographer and Editor. The Synopsis of the film. An affidavit from the writer for the authenticity of the film script. Production work should not be commenced without registering the film at the NFC. … If any changes of the film title, the payment of Rs. 3000/=should be made. If foreign artistes are in the cast/crew members, following payments should be made to the National Film Development Fund which is attached to the NFC. For a Major Role – Rs. 25,000.00 For a Supporting Role – Rs. 10,000.00
The National Film Corporation (NFC) proudly serves as the official authority for granting permission to international filmmakers seeking to shoot in this vibrant and diverse island.
